name: Iluvatar CoreX BI-V150 (Tiangai 150) cloud GPGPU training accelerator
memory_bandwidth_basis: None available. Iluvatar publishes no memory capacity, type, bus width or bandwidth for the BI-V150. The mirrorfrog.com spec sheet estimates 32-64 GB HBM2/HBM3 but explicitly labels this as 'estimated, same as TianGai 100' and notes 'Detailed specifications of TianGai 150 are not fully disclosed by official sources.'
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT: the BI-V150 is Iluvatar's second-generation cloud GPGPU training accelerator, released in 2023 as an upgrade to the BI-V100 (Tiangai 100). It uses the ivcore11 architecture on 7nm with 2.5D CoWoS packaging. The vendor publishes almost no specifications — the mirrorfrog.com page explicitly warns that 'Detailed specifications of TianGai 150 are not fully disclosed by official sources' and labels its FP16 (150-200 TFLOPS), INT8 (300-400 TOPS), memory capacity (32-64 GB) and TDP (275 W) entries as estimates. The moark.com page (a Chinese cloud provider) states 350 W peak power. The BI-V150 has participated in actual large-scale training deployments: Zhiyuan Research Institute's Aquila2-70B-Expr large model hybrid training used a 120-node BI-V100 cluster + 8-node BI-V150 cluster, reaching 85.3% of theoretical peak. The BI-V150 is significant because it represents Iluvatar's attempt to compete in the cloud training market, but the lack of vendor-published specifications makes it difficult to evaluate. Vendor is 'asic-other' because 'iluvatar' is not in the schema enum.
